sshPushWorkflow.description: Every generator pushes config over an interactive SSH shell (ssh2 Client), not NETCONF. The same sequence is used by both DIA generators (and by GPON — see the sibling knowledge file).
sshPushWorkflow.step: Enter a private candidate config session.
Write each generated "set ..." command line-by-line to the shell stream.
Validate the candidate config without committing.
Commit only after commit check succeeds; exits config mode afterward.
sshPushWorkflow.errorTrigger: Any of these substrings in accumulated stdout aborts the push and rejects the promise.
sshPushWorkflow.notes: - sshConfig is always { username, password } spread into the ssh2 .connect() call alongside host. - Devices are configured sequentially, never in parallel, so a failure on an earlier device (Metro switch) stops before touching downstream PE/BNG devices.

circuitIdConvention.description: Customer Circuit ID (CID) is normalized into a Junos virtual-circuit-id (vcId) used on both ends of the l2circuit pseudowire, and into a human-readable CID used inside interface description tags. Identical logic in both DIA generators.

rule.input: Any CID string; non-digit characters are stripped first.
rule.case: vcId = digits as-is; cidForDescription = "LTZ" + digits with leading "255" removed

peIdentifierConvention.description: Shortens a full device name to its first two dash-separated tokens for use inside neighbor ("nbr=") description tags, so descriptions stay stable even if a site suffix changes.
peIdentifierConvention.fallback: If the name has fewer than 2 dash-separated parts, return it unchanged.

networkAddressConvention.description: Converts a WAN gateway IP with CIDR into its network address, for use in "route-filter ... exact" policy terms (Junos route filters must match the network, not the host).

descriptionTagFormat.description: Interface unit descriptions embed a brace-delimited metadata tag consumed by other tooling (monitoring, inventory) elsewhere in this codebase.

l2circuitPattern.description: Both DIA services are delivered as an MPLS L2 circuit (pseudowire) between the Metro switch and a PE/BNG, configured symmetrically on both ends via `set protocols l2circuit neighbor <peer-ip> interface <local-intf> ...`. Common leaf statements: virtual-circuit-id, control-word, mtu, pseudowire-status-tlv. encapsulation-type and no-vlan-id-validate are added only on the With-Tag variant, since its local l2circuit endpoint carries an 802.1Q tag.

redundancyPattern.description: Both services accept an array of 2 PE/BNG devices ([primary, backup]) — the FIRST array element is always primary. Validate `peDevices.length >= 2` before building commands. In both DIA variants, the `backup-neighbor` statement is configured on the METRO side of the l2circuit (pointing at the backup PE/BNG); the PE/BNG side never carries backup-neighbor.

serviceType.name: DIA No Tag
serviceType.description: Untagged dedicated internet access circuit. Customer hands off untagged Ethernet at a dedicated Metro switch port, which is transported via l2circuit to a dedicated routed PE/BNG interface carrying the customer's WAN IP. No port-sharing concept exists here — every customer gets a fully dedicated physical interface on both ends.

device.label: Metro Switch
device.commandTemplate: set interfaces {intf} description "DIA: {customerName}| {cid} "
set interfaces {intf} speed auto
set interfaces {intf} mtu 9000
set interfaces {intf} encapsulation ethernet-ccc
set interfaces {intf} gigether-options auto-negotiation
set interfaces {intf} unit 0 description "{cat=DIA|nbr={nbrDescription}|Customer={customerName}|cid={cidForDescription}|Mbps={mbps}}"
set interfaces {intf} unit 0 statistics
set interfaces {intf} unit 0 family ccc
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.0 virtual-circuit-id {vcId}
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.0 control-word
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.0 mtu 1500
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.0 pseudowire-status-tlv
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.0 backup-neighbor {backupPeIp} virtual-circuit-id {vcId}
set routing-options static route {internalSubnet} next-hop {internalNextHop}

device.label: PE/BNG
device.note: Same command builder invoked once per device (both primary and backup receive identical config).
device.commandTemplate: set interfaces {peIntf} anchor-point {anchorPoint}
set interfaces {peIntf} unit 0 encapsulation ethernet-ccc
set interfaces {peIntf} unit 1 description "{cat=DIA|nbr={metroName}|Customer={customerName}|cid={cidForDescription}|Mbps={mbps}}"
set interfaces {peIntf} unit 1 layer2-policer input-policer {mbps}-MBPS-POLICER
set interfaces {peIntf} unit 1 layer2-policer output-policer {mbps}-MBPS-POLICER
set interfaces {peIntf} unit 1 family inet address {wanIp}
set interfaces {peIntf} unit 1 family inet6 dad-disable
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {metroIp} interface {peIntf}.0 virtual-circuit-id {vcId}
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {metroIp} interface {peIntf}.0 control-word
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {metroIp} interface {peIntf}.0 mtu 1500
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {metroIp} interface {peIntf}.0 pseudowire-status-tlv
set policy-options policy-statement RR-BGP-out term CONNECTED from route-filter {networkAddress} exact
device.note: networkAddress = getNetworkAddress(wanIp). Unit 1 (not 0) carries the routed customer traffic; unit 0 is the raw ccc encapsulation used only for the l2circuit endpoint.

serviceType.name: DIA With Tag
serviceType.description: Same intent as DIA No Tag, but the customer handoff is 802.1Q tagged and the PE/BNG side uses a shared "ps" (pseudo-interface / logical bundle) rather than a dedicated physical interface, so multiple VLAN customers can share one physical port on both ends. Because of this, the Metro switch side has TWO distinct command variants depending on whether the physical port is being used for the first time or is already shared with another customer — see <portVariants> below. The PE/BNG side has no such split; it is identical regardless of port sharing.

differencesFrom.difference: flexible-vlan-tagging + encapsulation flexible-ethernet-services instead of encapsulation ethernet-ccc directly on the interface.
Unit uses vlan-id {vlanId} and encapsulation vlan-ccc (802.1Q-tagged ccc) instead of plain unit 0 family ccc.
1800 instead of 1500 (extra headroom for the VLAN tag).
Always added (not conditional) — DIA With Tag always expects 2 PE/BNG devices.
Uses ps{psUnit} (logical/pseudo interface), not a dedicated physical peIntf. flexible-vlan-tagging is set on it.
encapsulation ethernet-ccc — used purely as the l2circuit endpoint (mirrors Metro's approach), separate from the numbered VLAN unit.
unit {psUnit} carries vlan-id {vlanId}, the layer2-policer pair, and family inet address — the routed/policed customer unit.
Adds encapsulation-type ethernet-vlan and no-vlan-id-validate (required whenever the local l2circuit endpoint interface is VLAN-tagged).

parameter.name: psUnit
parameter.note: Used both as the Metro VLAN unit number and the PE ps-interface number/unit number.

parameter.name: sharedPort
parameter.note: Selects which Metro command variant applies — see portVariants.

parameter.name: peIntf
parameter.note: Replaced by ps{psUnit}, derived rather than passed in directly.

portVariants.description: A single physical Metro interface can host multiple VLAN-tagged customers (different psUnit / vlanId per customer). The interface-level statements only need to be set ONCE per physical port; re-issuing them for every customer is unnecessary and, more importantly, would overwrite the description on an already-configured shared port. `sharedPort` tells the generator which of the two variants to emit.

variant.label: First customer on this physical port
variant.description: Full sequence: physical interface-level commands are issued first, then the per-customer VLAN unit and its l2circuit. Use this the first time a given Metro physical interface is used for DIA With Tag.
variant.commandTemplate: set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.{psUnit} virtual-circuit-id {vcId}
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.{psUnit} control-word
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.{psUnit} mtu 1800
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.{psUnit} pseudowire-status-tlv
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.{psUnit} backup-neighbor {backupPeIp} virtual-circuit-id {vcId}

variant.label: Additional customer on an already-configured physical port
variant.description: Short sequence: the 6 physical interface-level commands (description, flexible-vlan-tagging, speed, mtu, encapsulation, gigether-options) are SKIPPED entirely because a prior customer's VLAN unit already configured them on this port. Only the new customer's VLAN unit and its l2circuit are added — commands 7-16 from the dedicated-port variant, unchanged.
variant.commandTemplate: set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.{psUnit} virtual-circuit-id {vcId}
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.{psUnit} control-word
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.{psUnit} mtu 1800
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.{psUnit} pseudowire-status-tlv
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {primaryPeIp} interface {intf}.{psUnit} backup-neighbor {backupPeIp} virtual-circuit-id {vcId}
variant.caution: Caller is responsible for knowing that the physical port was already configured (e.g. by tracking prior provisioning in the inventory/database) — the generator itself does not probe the device to detect an existing configuration. Passing sharedPort=true for a port that was never configured will leave it without flexible-vlan-tagging/encapsulation and the commit will likely fail or the unit will be non-functional.

device.label: PE/BNG
device.note: Same command builder invoked once per device (both primary and backup receive identical config). No shared-port concept on this side — ps{psUnit} is always dedicated per customer.
device.commandTemplate: set interfaces ps{psUnit} anchor-point {anchorPoint}
set interfaces ps{psUnit} flexible-vlan-tagging
set interfaces ps{psUnit} mtu 9000
set interfaces ps{psUnit} unit 0 encapsulation ethernet-ccc
set interfaces ps{psUnit} unit {psUnit} description "{cat=DIA|nbr={metroIdentifier} {metroIntf}|Customer={customerName}|cid={cidForDescription}|Mbps={mbps}}"
set interfaces ps{psUnit} unit {psUnit} vlan-id {vlanId}
set interfaces ps{psUnit} unit {psUnit} layer2-policer input-policer {mbps}-MBPS-POLICER
set interfaces ps{psUnit} unit {psUnit} layer2-policer output-policer {mbps}-MBPS-POLICER
set interfaces ps{psUnit} unit {psUnit} family inet address {wanIp}
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {metroIp} interface ps{psUnit}.0 virtual-circuit-id {vcId}
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {metroIp} interface ps{psUnit}.0 control-word
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {metroIp} interface ps{psUnit}.0 mtu 1800
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {metroIp} interface ps{psUnit}.0 encapsulation-type ethernet-vlan
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {metroIp} interface ps{psUnit}.0 no-vlan-id-validate
set protocols l2circuit neighbor {metroIp} interface ps{psUnit}.0 pseudowire-status-tlv
set policy-options policy-statement RR-BGP-out term CONNECTED from route-filter {networkAddress} exact
set routing-options static route {internalSubnet} next-hop {internalNextHop}
set policy-options policy-statement RR-BGP-out term STATIC from route-filter {internalSubnet} exact
device.note: metroIdentifier = extractPeIdentifier(metroSwitch.name). PE side does NOT carry backup-neighbor (that lives on the Metro side).

pushOrder.step: Metro Switch (dedicated-port or shared-port variant per sharedPort flag)

axis.name: customer-facing VLAN tagging
axis.value: single tag, vlan-ccc on both ends

axis.name: port sharing
axis.value: not applicable — always a dedicated physical port
Metro physical port may be shared across customers; see portVariants (dedicated-port vs shared-port)

axis.name: backup-neighbor placement
axis.value: Metro side, conditional on backupPeIp being present

newServiceChecklist.item: Decide whether the customer handoff is routed (family inet + policer + BGP route-filter, as both DIA variants are) or pure L2 — see gpon-over-enterprise-templates.xml for the pure-L2 pattern.

Decide whether the access-facing physical port can be shared across customers. If yes, split the interface-level commands from the per-customer unit/l2circuit commands into two variants like dia-with-tag's portVariants, and add a boolean flag (sharedPort) the caller must set correctly.
Reuse processCid/extractPeIdentifier/getNetworkAddress helpers verbatim rather than re-deriving the logic.
Keep the brace-delimited description tag flavor for DIA-family services so downstream tooling parsing it does not need updating.

Follow the same SSH push workflow (configure private → commit check → commit and-quit) and expose both a push* (executes) and preview* (dry run, returns commands without connecting) function, matching the existing module.exports shape.
